title: Theme Authoring
subject: ui
summary: How to write a theme object. A theme is a TypeScript object conforming to the `Theme` type (`shared/libs/ui/types/theme.ts`).

purpose.intro: How to write a theme object. A theme is a TypeScript object conforming to the `Theme` type (`shared/libs/ui/types/theme.ts`).

snippets.code:
Theme
├── id, name
│
├── colors                         L1 primitive
│   ├── main (white, black)
│   ├── brand (1–4)
│   ├── status (success, info, warning, error → can reference flat)
│   ├── flat (11 accent colors)
│   └── semanticTokens (primary, secondary, accent, muted)
│
├── typography                     L1 primitive
│   ├── fonts (primary, secondary, quote, monoPrimary, monoSecondary)
│   └── types (18 scales, each: fontFamily, fontStyle, fontSizeMobile,
│              fontSizeDesktop, fontWeight, lineHeight, letterSpacing)
│
├── spacing                        L1 primitive (unit multiplier → xs..3xl)
├── radius                         L1 primitive (none, xs, sm, md, lg, xl, full)
├── effects                        L1 primitive (named effect presets)
├── transitions                    L1 primitive (duration + timing scales)
├── borderWidths                   L1 primitive (none → extraThick)
├── icons                          L1 primitive (set, sizes, weight)
│
├── modes                          Cross-cutting
│   └── colorScheme
│       └── each mode: background + foreground anchors + derivation params
│
├── families                       L2 — morphological family defaults
│   ├── surfaceContainer           (IS the base shape)
│   ├── elevatedOverlay            (surface + overlay extras)
│   ├── listContainer              (surface + row/cell/separator/alternating)
│   ├── interactiveControl         (surface wrapper)
│   ├── interactiveControlGroup    (surface wrapper)
│   ├── field                      (surface + placeholder/caret/obfuscation)
│   ├── shape                      (surface wrapper)
│   └── media                      (surface + objectFit/aspectRatio/overlay/filter)
│
├── elements                       L3 — element overrides (sparse deltas)
│
├── concepts                       L4 — product-specific semantic overrides
│   └── [conceptName]: { [target]: SurfaceContainerTokens + accent + contextual }
│
└── contextual                     L5 — parent → child overrides
    └── [parent]: { [child]: SurfaceContainerTokens }
        Keys are element names (e.g. 'sidebar', 'header', 'card')
        matching the keys in ElementTypes. NOT the full attribute
        value (not 'surface--sidebar').

reference.topic: Theme Object Structure › What the tree leaves out
reference.statement: Beside the levels above, a theme carries:

claims.text: `version` (the folder is `v<version>`), `type` (`wireframe` | `high-fidelity`), `kind` (`seed` | `product`).
`platform`: absent means web, `"mobile"` means mobile. A theme is for one platform; see Mobile.
`gradients`: named gradient definitions, referenced as `gradient-<name>` in a `background`.
`icons`: the icon set, the five icon sizes in px, the stroke weight.
`layouts`: the regions of a page, themed like elements; see Layouts.
`rules` (L6): cascade chains deeper than parent → child; see Concepts, contextual, rules.
`press` (mobile only): what a touch shows.

reference.statement: Every family, element and region is written with the same token shape, `SurfaceContainerTokens`. Each key is optional; write only what the level above does not already say.

claims.text: `boundary`: `border` (width, style, colour, per side), `radius` (all, per corner), `effect` (a named preset or layers), `outline` (web only), `margin`.

`interior`: `background` (a colour or a gradient), `backgroundAlpha`, `foreground`, `opacity`, `padding` (all, x, y, per side), `gap` (all, h, v), `separator`, `childAlign` (horizontal, vertical), `scrollbar` (web only).
`dimensionPosition`: `width`, `height`, `translateX`, `translateY`.

`defaultTypography`: `typographyType` (one of the 18 type scales), `textAlign`, `verticalAlign`, `textTransform`, `textDecoration`, `textEffect`. It never carries colour: colour is `interior.foreground`.
`tint`: the accent colour the pattern reads through `'tint'`.
`cursor` (web only), `smartBleed` (`false` | `normal` | `rounded` | `border` | `border-rounded`), `transition` (duration, timing).
`combined`: the entries per axis value, see The axes.

reference.statement: An element's look varies along axes. The markup carries the axis as an attribute; the theme writes what changes for each value. `shared/libs/ui/types/axes.ts` holds the values, `shared/libs/ui/types/elements.ts` says which axes each element takes.

claims.text: An element not listed for an axis ignores that axis. `concept` is on every element and is never listed.
`emphasis`, `status`, `state` and `position` are written as `combined` entries on a surface: `{ where: { <axis>: <value> }, partialSurface: {…} }`. A `where` with several keys is a combination.
The engine emits the `combined` entries in the order they are written. Write emphasis, then status, then state, then the combinations, so the later ones win.
`scale` is not a `combined` key: it is authored in `sizes`, see Size Variants.
Emphasis carries the pattern; status carries the colour over it; state carries the delta while it lasts. See Tint Pattern.

imagesAndDiagrams.value:
| axis      | values                                                        | carries                                   | written as              |
|-----------|---------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|-------------------------|
| emphasis  | hero, primary, secondary, tertiary, quiet                     | the pattern: filled, outlined, ghost      | where: { emphasis }     |
| status    | neutral, info, success, warning, error, destructive           | the tint over the pattern                 | where: { status }       |
| state     | hover, active, focus, selected, disabled, loading             | the delta while the state lasts           | where: { state }        |
|           | mobile: no hover; long-pressed in its place; swiped on rows   |                                           |                         |
| position  | first, last, only, middle, even, odd (sibling order)          | edges and separators of a row in a list   | where: { position }     |
| scale     | 3xs 2xs xs sm md lg xl 2xl 3xl (default md)                   | padding, typography, icon size; no colour | sizes: { md: {…} }      |
| concept   | a free name                                                   | a product meaning                         | concepts (L4)           |

snippets.caption: typescript

examples.text: A control: the base, two emphases, a status, a combination, and the states.

reference.statement: Eight families. Every element belongs to one; the family block is where most of a theme is written. `surfaceContainer` is the base every other family inherits; the others add the tokens below beside their `surface`.

claims.text: `surfaceContainer` (`surface--…`): card, panel, section, header, footer, badge, avatar, tile, alert, separator, spinner, skeleton, progress… Written bare: its tokens are the surface itself.
`elevatedOverlay` (`overlay--…`): dialog, drawer, popover, tooltip, toast, sheet, menu. Adds `overlay`: `scrimColor`, `scrimOpacity`, `scrimBlur`, `entranceAnimation`, `exitAnimation`.

`interactiveControl` (`control--…`): button, icon-button, chip, toggle, checkbox, radio, tab-trigger, sidebar-item… Adds `startIcon`, `endIcon` (each a surface). `switch` has its own shape: `track` and `thumb`.
`interactiveControlGroup` (`control-group--…`): tab-bar, breadcrumb, pagination, button-group, toggle-group, sidebar. A `surface` only.

`field` (`field--…`): input, textarea, select, combobox, date-picker, otp, phone… Adds `startIcon`, `endIcon`, `placeholderColor`, `placeholderOpacity`, `caretColor`, `obfuscation` (character, letterSpacing, fontSize).
`listContainer` (`list--…`): list, accordion, menu, tree. Adds `row`, `cell`, `alternating` (surfaces) and `separator` (a surface with `height`, `width`).
`table` elements (`table--…`): root, header, body, row, cell, footer. A surface each; `tableRow` and `tableFooterCell` add `alternating`.
`shape` (`shape--…`): icon, logo, decorative. A `surface` only.
`media` (`media--…`): image, video, embed. Adds `objectFit`, `objectPosition`, `aspectRatio`, `overlay` (colour, opacity, blur), `filter` (grayscale, brightness, contrast, blur).
The elements of each family, their axes and their platform are the rows of `shared/libs/ui/types/elements.ts`; the names people write are in the markup dictionary.

reference.statement: The regions of a page are themed in `layouts`, keyed by the camelCase region name (`pageHeader` → `layout="page-header"`). A region carries a `surface` and the dimensions the theme owns.

claims.text: `layouts.surface` is the default of every region, as `families.surfaceContainer` is for elements.
Headers (`pageHeader`, `secondPageHeader`, `mainHeader`, `secondMainHeader`, `mainFooter`): `height`, and `sm`/`md`/`lg` heights for `scale`.
Sidebars (`leftSidebar`, `rightSidebar`, `contextPanel`, `shellNav`): `width`, and `sm`/`md`/`lg` widths. `leftSidebar` adds `widthCollapsed` and a `collapsed` surface.
`container`: `maxWidth` per scale `xs`…`xl`. `dialog`: `maxWidth` per `sm`/`md`/`lg`. `sheet`: `size` per `sm`/`md`/`lg`/`full`. Their visual tokens stay in `elements`.
`scrollArea`: the `scrollbar` only.
`layouts.emphasis` has two values, `primary` and `secondary`: a region's shade over its own base, for a region carrying `emphasis`. The region's own rule keeps its border edge.
Regions do not take `status`, `state` or `combined`.

snippets.caption: typescript

claims.text: Derived colours the engine computes: `gray-50`…`gray-950` (from the mode's background and foreground), `gray-pure-<step>` (mode independent), `brand-<n>-light` | `brand-<n>-dark`, `brand-<n>-gray-<step>` (a brand-tinted gray), `status-<x>-light` | `status-<x>-dark`, `smart-bw`, `tint`. The amounts are the mode's `derivation`.
A `background` may be a gradient: `gradient-<name>`, defined in `gradients` as one layer or a stack of layers (linear, radial, conic).

reference.statement: Theme token values can reference colors by name:

imagesAndDiagrams.value:
| Type | Examples |
|------|----------|
| Primitive | `'main-white'`, `'brand-1'`, `'status-error'`, `'flat-blue'` |
| Derived | `'gray-200'`, `'brand-1-light'`, `'status-error-dark'` |
| Semantic | `'primary'`, `'secondary'`, `'accent'`, `'muted'` |
| Mode anchors | `'background'`, `'foreground'` (resolved from active color mode, not semantic tokens) |
| Special | `'tint'` (current tint value), `'smart-bw'` (auto black/white) |
| CSS | `'transparent'`, `'currentColor'`, `'inherit'` |
| Raw hex | `'#ff0000'` (escape hatch, avoid when possible) |

reference.topic: Color References › Which colour to write

claims.text: A surface's fill is `'background'`; its text is `'foreground'`. The two swap in dark mode.
Text on a coloured fill (a brand, a status) is `'smart-bw'`.
`'main-white'` and `'main-black'` are written only where the colour must not swap: the mode anchors and the shadows.
A tinted ground is a brand-tinted gray (`'brand-1-gray-50'`), with the amount in the mode's `grayColorMixPercentage`.

reference.statement: Each color mode defines background/foreground anchors and derivation parameters. The engine computes gray scales, brand light/dark, status light/dark from these.

claims.text: Concepts apply to both elements and layouts. `concept="dashboard"` on a shell → the theme overrides `mainContent` background for dashboard pages.

reference.statement: Two more levels, for what a family or an element cannot say on its own.

claims.text: L5 `contextual`: parent → child, keyed by element names (`sidebar: { button: {…} }`), the child typed as its own family shape. For a child that looks different inside one parent.

L6 `rules`: a `chain` of segments, each `{ key, concept? }` (an element, a layout or a family name, with the concept the node carries), and the `tokens` to apply at its end. For anything deeper than parent → child, or concepts on several nodes of the chain.
Neither repairs what a family should have set. An override written here to fix a general look is a family value in the wrong place.

snippets.caption: typescript

claims.text: Default scale when absent: `md`.
The scale values are `3xs 2xs xs sm md lg xl 2xl 3xl`; a size entry is a `partialSurface` and an `icon` size.
Scale changes padding, typography and icon size, never colour. It is not a `combined` key.

reference.statement: Elements the table gives a `scale` define their sizes in `sizes`, keyed by scale. A family may author `sizes` too: every element of the family inherits them, an element overrides with its own.

snippets.caption: typescript

reference.statement: Emphasis defines the pattern and sets `tint`; status overrides `tint` only, so the pattern keeps its shape and changes colour. Both are written as `combined` entries, see The axes.

snippets.caption: typescript

reference.statement: A mobile theme is the same type with `platform: "mobile"`: the same core, families, elements and cascade, in mobile's shapes, plus what only a phone has.

claims.text: No `hover`, `cursor`, `scrollbar` or `outline`. Writing one in a mobile theme does not compile.

States: the shared ones (`active`, `focus`, `selected`, `disabled`, `loading`) plus `long-pressed` (in the place of `hover`) and `swiped` (a row slid sideways). The elements table says which an element takes (`mobileState`).

Regions in `layouts`: `screen`, `appBar`, `body` (the one that scrolls), `actionBar`, `tabBar`, `drawer` (with `width`), each with a `surface` and `safeArea` edges; bars have `height` with `sm`/`md`/`lg`; `dialog` and `sheet` sizes.
`press`: `opacityDim` (iOS) and `ripple` (Android: `color`, `borderless`).

A mobile theme addresses only the elements the table gives to mobile (`platform`). Concepts, contextual, rules and gradients are not emitted by the mobile engine; the build lists them as `unsupported`.
A product's web and mobile apps wear two themes. To share values, the mobile theme imports them from the web theme (`colors: webTheme.colors`).

reference.statement: A theme compiles to one file per platform; a project points at one theme per platform.

claims.text: `pnpm theme:build` builds every theme: a web theme to `themes/<id>/v<n>/generated/<id>.css`, a mobile theme to `generated/<id>.native.json`.
A project names its themes in `shared/themes/active.json`: the web theme at the top, the mobile theme under `mobile`. UX/UI → theme sets each.
A design never names a theme. `active.json` is the one pointer.
The design system is the test: walk foundations, components, patterns, layouts and the check pages after each level, in light and in dark.
